subject: ProofPoint AI — Connectivity acceptance & environment checklist
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@proofpoint.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Roberts <aisha.roberts@proofpoint.ai>, procurement@proofpoint.ai
Date: 2028-03-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — MAP & connectivity checklist

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team was impressed with the throughput and the cost controls. We want to formalize the mutual action plan so we can get a PoC running against our staging environment next week. To move fast, I need a clear checklist we can hand to our infra and procurement teams. Specifically: 

- How do we receive API keys and what environment (org) will they be scoped to?
- What exact IP ranges need to be allowlisted?
- What are the steps and lead times for VPC peering? We're on GCP (project: proofpoint-staging, vpc: pp-staging-vpc).
- Any required firewall rules or load-balancer config you need us to change for short-lived tests?

Can you produce an acceptance checklist (technical gates + who owns each item)? If you can attach a draft MAP spreadsheet, that would help. Procurement wants estimated close timing so they can align PO dates.

Thanks —
Liam
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
ProofPoint AI

---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@proofpoint.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — MAP & connectivity checklist

Liam —

Appreciate the fast follow-up. I've attached a working MAP (redwood-map-v0.3.xlsx) with milestones and ownership. High-level plan below; I mapped expected lead times and acceptance criteria so your infra and procurement teams can act in parallel.

Milestone 1 — Org & API Keys (owner: Redwood / Monica)
- Action: Create customer org mapping in Redwood console and provision two short-lived API keys (staging/test).
- Acceptance: Keys issue and successful token-auth curl to /v1/health endpoint from your IP (sample below).
- Lead time: 24–48 hours once we have confirmation of the admin email and org slug.

Milestone 2 — IP allowlist (owner: ProofPoint / Liam + Redwood)
- Action: Provide the external egress IPs for your test runners and the CIDR ranges for staging. We will return the exact Redwood egress IPs to add.
- Acceptance: Your staging runner can call /v1/health and /v1/generate with <200ms auth handshake and no TLS blocks.
- Lead time: Your infra config ~2 business days; verification same day.

Milestone 3 — VPC peering (owner: ProofPoint infra + Redwood infra / Soojin)
- Action: Open a peering request. We support GCP peering. Need: project ID, VPC name, subnet CIDRs, and a point-of-contact for routing.
- Acceptance: Route propagation confirmed and test pod in your VPC can reach the Redwood peered endpoint over private IPs.
- Lead time: Typically 3–5 business days (depends on routing review).

Milestone 4 — Security & procurement checklist (owner: ProofPoint procurement / Aisha)
- Action: Sign SOW/PO or confirm the procurement timing and any required NDA/clauses. We will provide SOC2 artifacts and an access log sample.
- Acceptance: PO issued or purchase timing committed; SOW countersigned for the PoC term.

Technical test snippets (for your infra team):
- Curl to validate auth: 
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <STAGING_KEY>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health

Next steps from our side: Soojin will reach out with the peering template and exact Redwood egress IPs to add to your allowlist. Karthik will coordinate any intake for higher-throughput test profiles.

I can be your primary contact for milestones 1 and 4. Proposed close for PoC activation: 2028-04-05. If that works, we will target a staging smoke test the afternoon of 2028-04-06.

Attaching: redwood-map-v0.3.xlsx (MAP draft).

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@proofpoint.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-28T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — MAP & connectivity checklist

Hi Liam —

Quick technical notes to help your network team configure the allowlist/peering: 
- Required outbound from your test runners to Redwood: 443/TCP to our public API and, if peered, the private IPs we'll provide.
- Redwood egress IPs for staging tests (add to allowlist): 34.201.112.45, 34.201.112.46 (we'll provide a signed list in the peering doc).
- Peering details we need from you: GCP project ID (proofpoint-staging), VPC name (pp-staging-vpc), VPC CIDRs (e.g., 10.40.0.0/16), and preferred subnet for testing.
- Firewall/NAT guidance: Ensure your NAT gateway allows outbound TLS SNI for api.redwood.ai. For private peering, create a route to the peered IP block; avoid overlapping CIDRs.

Small test plan:
1) Create a small pod in your staging cluster with curl and a staging key.
2) Run curl -v to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health and capture TLS handshake time.
3) Run a 5-minute generation load (10 RPS) to validate token and KV cache behavior.

If you can share the initial peering request (we prefer a single email with the project/VPC details) I'll start our internal peering ticket and loop in infra. I'm copying a minimal peering template in the attached MAP.

Soojin
Infra & Private Deployments Lead
Redwood Inference

---

From: Aisha Roberts <aisha.roberts@proofpoint.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@proofpoint.ai>, procurement@proofpoint.ai
Date: 2028-03-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — MAP & connectivity checklist

Monica / Soojin —

Thanks for the draft MAP and the clear milestones. A few procurement/ops notes from our side: 
- Procurement has a tentative PO approval window targeting 2028-04-03, pending final SOW redlines. I'll upload the network diagram we talked about (attached).
- Our infra team confirms GCP project proofpoint-staging and VPC pp-staging-vpc; CIDR block is 10.40.0.0/16, and we can allocate a /24 for testing (10.40.10.0/24).
- Peering POC: Kevin Marsh (kevin.marsh@proofpoint.ai) will be the routing contact. He can accept the peering template and follow the RFC steps.

Question for Redwood: Do you require a service account from our side for authenticated peering setup, or will a simple CIDR + shared routing table be enough? Also, can you confirm whether logs for PoC calls are retained for 14 or 30 days (we have a compliance window to respect)?

Aisha Roberts
Head of Procurement
ProofPoint AI

Attachment: proofpoint-network-diagram.png

---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Roberts <aisha.roberts@proofpoint.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@proofpoint.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-29T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — MAP & connectivity checklist

Thanks Aisha —

Answers: 
- Service account: Not required for the initial peering template. For full private link integration we sometimes request a read-only service account to validate routing via the GCP API, but for a standard VPC peering CIDR+routes is sufficient for the PoC. We'll document either path in the peering ticket.
- Logs retention: For the PoC environment we default to 14 days for request logs; we can extend to 30 days if needed (flag this in the MAP and we will update the retention policy before you run sensitive tests).

Proposed schedule based on your PO window: 
- 2028-03-29: ProofPoint provides final peering details and Kevin's contact (we have those; thanks).
- 2028-03-30 (EOD): Redwood issues staging API keys once we receive the org admin email.
- 2028-04-03: Procurement finalizes PO (target).
- 2028-04-05: PoC activation (dry run).
- 2028-04-06: Staging smoke test (afternoon) — target for turnkey verification.

I'll create a HubSpot activity for 2028-04-03 to track PO confirmation and link it in the MAP (see link). If the procurement timeline slips, we can run a limited internal PoC with time-limited keys to validate integration while paperwork completes.

Best,
Monica

---

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@proofpoint.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Roberts <aisha.roberts@proofpoint.ai>, Kevin Marsh <kevin.marsh@proofpoint.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-30T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — MAP & connectivity checklist

Monica / team —

All good from our side. Kevin will submit the peering request this afternoon and procurement is lining up the PO for the 2028-04-03 window. Please go ahead and stage the MAP and issue test keys to staging-admin@proofpoint.ai when ready. We'll test the health endpoint and run the 10 RPS smoke profile on 2028-04-06 afternoon as proposed.

I'll mark the HubSpot link and keep you posted on any internal blockers. Thanks for the clear ownership — looks like we're aligned.

-Liam
